paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Фигурата е линейна диаграма, която илюстрира зависимостта между "Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)" и "Rank". Ос X е обозначена като "Rank" и използва логаритмична скала, като етикетите са разположени при стойности 4, 16, 64 и 256, които са равномерно разпределени по логаритмичния интервал. Ос Y е обозначена като "Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)" и използва линейна скала, с диапазон от 0.0 до 8.0, с етикети на интервали от 4.0 (0.0, 4.0, 8.0). Визуално са представени четири точки, свързани с черна плътна линия. Всеки от четирите данни е маркиран с жълт квадратен маркер, който има вертикални грешки (error bars), показващи несигурността. При Rank = 4, стойността на Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA) е около 1.0. При Rank = 16, стойността е почти същата – около 1.0, с леко по-ниско значение. При Rank = 64, стойността нараства до около 4.0. При Rank = 256, стойността достига около 7.0. Линията показва почти хоризонтален участък между Rank 4 и 16, след което има значително нарастване между Rank 16 и 256, с по-бързо увеличение между 64 и 256. Грешките са най-големи при Rank = 256 и най-малки при Rank = 4 и 16.
model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the Hessian trace values (scaled by 10⁻⁵) for COPA as a function of the rank of QLoRA adapters. The x-axis, labeled "Rank," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick marks at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, labeled "Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)," is on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 8.0, with tick marks at 0.0, 4.0, and 8.0. A single black line connects four data points, each marked with an orange square and vertical error bars, indicating uncertainty. At a rank of 4, the trace value is approximately 1.0; at rank 16, it remains nearly constant at about 1.0; at rank 64, it increases to approximately 4.0; and at rank 256, it reaches approximately 7.0. The trend shows that the Hessian trace increases with rank, suggesting that higher-rank adapters converge to sharper minima, while lower-rank adapters (e.g., rank 16) achieve flatter minima, which correlates with lower generalization errors as noted in the caption.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt die Hessian-Trace-Werte (multipliziert mit 10⁻⁵) für das COPA-Dataset in Abhängigkeit vom Rang (Rank) der Adapter in einem QLoRA-Modell. Die x-Achse ist logarithmisch skaliert und beschriftet mit „Rank“, wobei die Werte 4, 16, 64 und 256 angegeben sind, die jeweils durch gleichmäßige Abstände auf der logarithmischen Skala repräsentiert werden. Die y-Achse ist linear skaliert und beschriftet mit „Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)“, mit einem Wertebereich von 0.0 bis 8.0, wobei die Tick-Beschriftungen in Schritten von 4.0 angezeigt werden. Eine einzelne schwarze Linie verbindet vier Datenpunkte, die jeweils mit orangefarbenen Quadraten und vertikalen Fehlern markiert sind. Bei einem Rank von 4 beträgt der Trace-Wert etwa 1.0 × 10⁻⁵, bei einem Rank von 16 bleibt er nahezu konstant bei etwa 1.0 × 10⁻⁵. Ab einem Rank von 64 steigt der Wert auf etwa 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ an und erreicht bei einem Rank von 256 einen Wert von etwa 7.0 × 10⁻⁵. Die Linie verläuft somit zunächst flach und steigt dann stark an, wobei die Fehlerbalken bei jedem Punkt eine geringe Unsicherheit anzeigen.
